operation_details.item: The user prefers dense technical specification language with exact pixel counts and engineering jargon in creative briefs instead of mood and visual metaphor.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Good morning! What are you working on today—another client deliverable or something more exploratory?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I’m tightening the brief for a cultural identity project. I want the visual language to feel crafted and specific rather than defaulting to generic minimalism.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That sounds promising. Are you drawing from a particular cultural reference set, or are you building the visual system through custom lettering, texture, and image treatment?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: A mix of archival patterns and contemporary street graphics. I’m also making the lettering by hand so the system retains some human irregularity.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Nice contrast. How do you want the client brief to describe that direction—through mood and visual metaphor, or through production-ready constraints?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I prefer dense technical specification language: exact pixel counts, grid intervals, color values, export dimensions, and engineering-style implementation notes instead of mood language or visual metaphor.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it. That should make the deliverables easier to execute consistently, especially if multiple people will be producing assets. Are you defining the specs for print, digital, or both?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Both. I’m starting with a 1440-pixel digital layout and a print master, then I’ll document the scaling rules so the custom details don’t get flattened across formats.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that In creative briefs for designers, I want dense technical specification language with exact pixel counts and engineering jargon instead of mood, audience, or visual metaphor.
